subject: Selecting smoothness parameter alpha for the Matern cov fn

messages.author: 46d7a4fa0dad1078
messages.subject: Selecting smoothness parameter alpha for the Matern cov fn
parts:
Good day,

Based on some exploratory data analysis, I found that my smoothness parameter for the Matern covariance function is typically estimated above 40.  In the function inla.spde2.matern(), I have noticed that alpha has a restriction on the interval from 0 to 2.  Is there any way to increase this alpha value, or is it something that may be available in the future?  I realize increasing alpha results in less sparsity in Q thus longer computation times, but for my application I think the results would be more meaningful if I could set alpha higher to achieve smoother results.  Any insight or suggestions are much appreciated, thank you for your help!

Steve

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Selecting smoothness parameter alpha for the Matern cov fn
parts:
Hi,

Smoothness above around 4-5 is very hard to distinguish from infinity (which corresponds to a “squared exponential” covariance, so I wouldn’t hold too much weight on the value 40, much larger and much smaller values will produce very similar fields. But as you say, smoothness 1 (spde order 2) can be noticeably less smooth.
Due to the way inla is coded internally, the easiest way to access smoother spde model is to build your own precision matrix as part of an “rgeneric” model. That is how e.g. the “barrier model” has been implemented, and how we are working to get more general spatial-temporal models.  I think there are some rgeneric examples linked from r-inla.org. You can follow the Lindgren et al 2011 paper for the definition of the precision for the higher order models, and use inla.mesh.fem() to access the needed c0, g1, g2, g3, etc matrices.

Finn

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Selecting smoothness parameter alpha for the Matern cov fn
parts:
the higher the smoothness, the less sparse the matrices will be, and
the computation time is higher.

if you compare RW1 and RW2

> INLA:::inla.rw(5, order=1)
5 x 5 sparse Matrix of class "dgTMatrix"

[1,] 1 -1 . . .
[2,] -1 2 -1 . .
[3,] . -1 2 -1 .
[4,] . . -1 2 -1
[5,] . . . -1 1
> INLA:::inla.rw(5, order=2)
5 x 5 sparse Matrix of class "dgTMatrix"

[1,] 1 -2 1 . .
[2,] -2 5 -4 1 .
[3,] 1 -4 6 -4 1
[4,] . 1 -4 5 -2
[5,] . . 1 -2 1


the cost is about (2/1)^2 = 4 times higher.
